scope: Finite native AWS observations on owned 1-GiB synthetic snapshots; not a general parity claim.

fixtures.sharing_data.json: Immediate share/revoke observations and first delivered audit; propagation-sensitive.
fixtures.sharing_data_settled.json: Owner-readable controls; private sharing, IAM/KMS, revoke/reset, and two-account delivered audit.
fixtures.sharing_data_lookup.json: Explicit shared/deleted snapshot IDs and service-malformed controls.
fixtures.sharing_data_tags.json: Recipient-local tags and a 65-second revoke window.
fixtures.sharing_data_tags_settled.json: Recipient-local tags after confirmed empty permissions and a 300-second revoke window.
fixtures.sharing_data_pairs.json: Shared lineage, cross-owner unrelated pairs, one inaccessible endpoint, public ownership distinctions.
fixtures.sharing_data_public_token.json: Previously valid recipient block token after public+private and public-only sharing.
fixtures.sharing_data_limits.json: 500/501 duplicate self-account additions in canonical and legacy forms; no resource reprovisioning.

contracts.private_visibility: Recipient explicit DescribeSnapshots returns InvalidSnapshot.NotFound; EBS List/Get and shared-parent Start return ResourceNotFoundException/SNAPSHOT_NOT_FOUND before sharing.
contracts.private_sharing: After propagation, recipient List/Get succeed and return the synthetic owner block. An owner-minted token also works for the recipient.
contracts.shared_parent: StartSnapshot with a privately shared parent returns ResourceNotFoundException/SNAPSHOT_NOT_FOUND even while recipient List/Get succeed, for plain and CMK-encrypted sources. No cross-account child was created; inheritance/child-deletion independence is therefore inapplicable.
contracts.iam: Account sharing does not replace identity/session authority: no identity allow, implicit session deny and explicit EBS action denies reject reads. ResourceAccount=source owner allows shared reads; ResourceAccount=requester denies. Denying ec2:DescribeSnapshots does not deny EBS reads.
contracts.kms: Encrypted shared reads without CMK trust, or with sole session Deny kms:Decrypt, return ResourceNotFoundException/DEPENDENCY_RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND with message KMS key not found. Key-policy trust without grants permits reads. Sole Deny GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext or CreateGrant does not prevent reads.
contracts.revocation: After settled revoke/reset, List/Get reject with SNAPSHOT_NOT_FOUND even using a previously valid token. Re-sharing makes that same token usable again. EC2 metadata and EBS data propagation are independently observable.
contracts.discovery: For an explicitly shared source, recipient OwnerIds=[source owner], RestorableByUserIds=self and RestorableByUserIds=[numeric recipient] include it; OwnerIds=self and RestorableByUserIds=[numeric source owner] do not. Explicit-ID lookup after settled revoke is InvalidSnapshot.NotFound.
contracts.mutation: Sharing does not allow recipient source delete/permission mutation, PutSnapshotBlock, or CompleteSnapshot. Recipient CreateTags is a separate account-local namespace and does not mutate owner tags.
contracts.tags: Recipient DescribeTags and tag-filtered DescribeSnapshots use recipient-local tags. Shared CreateTags ec2:Owner and aws:ResourceAccount conditions match source owner, not requester. After settled revoke, DescribeSnapshots/CreateTags deny visibility but DescribeTags retains recipient tags and DeleteTags still removes them.
contracts.changed_blocks: Both owner snapshots in one privately shared lineage can be compared by recipient. Valid accessible cross-owner independent snapshots reject with ValidationException/UNRELATED_SNAPSHOTS. One revoked endpoint causes SNAPSHOT_NOT_FOUND in either argument order.
contracts.public: Owner List/Get remain usable on own public snapshots. Recipient List and Get reject with ValidationException/INVALID_SNAPSHOT_ID: Public snapshots are not supported. This applies even when an explicit private grant coexists, and even when reusing a token issued before the public flag.
contracts.modification_limit: 500 duplicate self-account Add entries succeed in both canonical and legacy forms without permission mutation; 501 fail InvalidParameterValue: Modification size must not be greater than 500. This proves counting before duplicate/self no-op elimination for the tested Add forms.
contracts.ebs_audit: Positive caller/owner paired GetSnapshotBlock records share sharedEventID; paired records also exist for shared-source rejected StartSnapshot, CompleteSnapshot and PutSnapshotBlock, including KMS-failed Get. Owner userIdentity is AWSAccount, caller is AssumedRole. Both EBS copies use requester accountId in resources, independently of snapshot owner and recipientAccountId. Caller List/ListChanged records were delivered; their missing owner copies do not establish absence.
contracts.kms_audit: Positive owner/caller DescribeKey and Decrypt pairs have invokedBy=ebs.amazonaws.com and source snapshot encryptionContext aws:ebs:id. Owner identity is AWSAccount, caller is AssumedRole, recipientAccountId follows the delivery account. Mixed Get/List sessions do not identify which one caused a particular KMS child event.

boundaries: Observed propagation windows are not service latency guarantees.
Finite delivered CloudTrail records are positive evidence only; omissions are not absence claims.
The broad documentation note denying owner delivery for shared EBS data is contradicted by captured paired Get/Put records.
Cross-account EBS aws:ResourceTag owner-versus-recipient namespace was not probed because snapshots had already been cleaned when requested; no reprovisioning was authorized.
Only Add duplicate-entry limit forms were measured, not every combined Add/Remove size or validation-precedence permutation.
